Getting started

a00_introduction.Rmd

Cohort2Trajectory builds patient histories from a target cohort and state cohorts. The target cohort defines when each patient is observed. The state cohorts supply the clinical intervals. You decide what those intervals mean and how overlaps should be handled.

This example uses local data, so you do not need a database connection. For an OMOP database, see Import cohort data.

Supply the cohort intervals

Patient 001 is observed for 14 days. State A covers the first week and state B covers the second. Patient 002 is observed for ten days and has no state records.

input <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("001", "001", "001", "002"),
  cohort_definition_id = c("0", "A", "B", "0"),
  cohort_start_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-08", "2020-01-01"
  )),
  cohort_end_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-14", "2020-01-07", "2020-01-14", "2020-01-10"
  ))
)

"0" identifies target-cohort rows. Other values are state labels. Dates include both endpoints. Keep identifiers as text if leading zeros matter.

Configure, import and generate

Choose seven-day cycles and put B ahead of A if they overlap. The input here does not contain any overlap, but specifying the rule makes it explicit.

studyPath <- tempfile("c2t-getting-started-")
dir.create(studyPath)

study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "Example",
  pathToStudy = studyPath,
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = input,
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 7
)
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)

Read the result 

knitr::kable(trajectories[c(
  "subject_id", "state_label", "state_start_date", "state_end_date"
)], row.names = FALSE)
subject_id state_label state_start_date state_end_date
001 START 2020-01-01 2020-01-01
001 A 2020-01-01 2020-01-07
001 B 2020-01-08 2020-01-14
001 EXIT 2020-01-15 2020-01-15
002 START 2020-01-01 2020-01-01
002 OUT OF COHORT 2020-01-01 2020-01-07
002 OUT OF COHORT 2020-01-08 2020-01-10
002 EXIT 2020-01-11 2020-01-11

Patient 002 is still included. Both cycles have the label OUT OF COHORT because no state was supplied. That label means an unresolved cycle, not a loss of observation. The second cycle ends on January 10, the target-cohort end date, rather than being extended to a full week.

START is the start boundary. EXIT is the day after the last cycle and does not add an observed day. Neither is a clinical state.

The function returns the trajectory table and saves it under Example/Data/patientDataDiscrete.csv. The completed analysis settings are saved under Example/Settings/analysisSettings.rds.
